text.what: A small pink bean grown in the Santa Maria Valley and almost nowhere else, cooked with bacon or ham, garlic, chilli and a little tomato, and served in a bowl beside the beef.
text.story: Considered indigenous to this valley; a cross between a pink bean and a small white one. Betteravia Farms began growing them commercially in 1972, and a handful of local brands still supply the barbecue trade.

kin.as: The only ground that grows them at scale.

recipes.title: Pinquito beans, as the tradition describes them
recipes.note: ingredients only: the seasoning varies house to house and no free-to-use recipe was found for the method
